document.abstract: Forecasting the events of the Digital Decade to come is a risky business but very worthwhile to attempt. It's risky because there can be quantum jumps in technology at any time. For example, at the time the transistor was invented everyone expected the continued evolution of vacuum tubes and few, if any, foresaw solidstate circuitry. The best that a forecaster can do is acknowledge that such surprises are possible and then use existing facts and trands to build up a surprise-free forecast that is not too conservative.

authors.bio: William M. Webster received the B.S. Degree in Physics from Union College in 1945 and a Ph.D. Degree in Electrical Engineering from Princeton University in 1954. Since 1946, he has held various positions in research and development and technical management with RCA Corp. At present, he is Vice President, RCA Laboratories, David Sarnoff Research Center. Mr. Webster is a Fellow of the IEEE, a member of the National Academy of Engineering, and a member of Sigma Xi.
